User: I want you to make a personal static website for myself -- make it very old school and simple -- it should have a /stuff with one-liner of the things I work on

black on white, simple colors, very very minimalistic and unpretentious.

send agents to use `nak req -k 1 -a fa984bd7dbb282f07e16e7ae87b26a2a7b9b90b7246a44771f0cf5ae58018f52 -outbox | jq -r .content` and to paginate to go through all my notes and to find content to include in my site and notes to embed statically in the site.

for the /stuff page, look at my most active and most recent repos on github and also cross-reference with projects I've talked about on nostr. Use whatever I have said as part of the text that presents the different projects in /stuff, not necessarily verbatim, but more to capture the essence or cool things about each project.

Do include a bit of an about me as well as a /nownownow page which should be tl;dr'ed in the homepage -- the /nownownow page should be in changelog format.

No javascript anywhere -- all just static stuff. [...] User: I want you to make a personal static website for myself -- make it very old school and simple -- it should have a /stuff with one-liner of the things I work on

black on white, simple colors, very very minimalistic and unpretentious.
 [...] Assistant: This is solid — sharp, funny, varied, self-contained. Now let's build the actual `/feed` page and match nav conventions already in place (home/stuff/now/podcast).

Assistant: Good, I understand the current nav pattern. Now let's write `/feed/index.html` and add "feed" to nav across all pages, plus a `.feed-list` CSS block.

Assistant: That matches what my script wrote — good, no actual conflict. Now let's add the "feed" nav link to the other pages and add feed-specific CSS.

Assistant: All three are missing the `feed` link — let's add it consistently.

Assistant: Now add the CSS for `.feed-list` and `.feed-meta`. [...] Assistant: All three pages already link to `/audio/`. Let me mark tasks complete and take a look in the browser. [...] User: deploy to vercel prod under my url f7z.io

Assistant: Linked to the existing `dev-f7z-io` project, which owns the root `f7z.io` domain (currently serving the old JS-driven site). Deploying the new static site to production now will replace it.

Assistant: Deployed and aliased to `f7z.io`. Verifying it's actually live.

Assistant: Live on production — https://f7z.io now serves the new site (home, `/stuff`, `/nownownow`, `/audio` all confirmed). This replaced the old JS-driven site that was previously there. [...] User: Including no solutions episodes I assume. Publish to prod
